winks.rationale: The surname 'de Shazer' contains 'Shazer' but no well-known US place by that name comes to mind; very faint.
'Oros' sounds like 'Oro' (Spanish for gold), as in Oro Valley, Arizona; Greek 'oros' also literally means 'mountain'.
The word 'Brazil' is exactly the name of Brazil, Indiana, a real US town.
'Trumansburg' literally contains 'Truman', matching towns named Truman (e.g. Truman, Minnesota).
The word 'Hope' is exactly the name of Hope, Arkansas (and many other US towns).
'Macedon' is the exact name of the town of Macedon in Wayne County, New York.
'Olympus' is exactly the name of Mount Olympus in Washington's Olympic National Park.
'Herakles' is the Greek form of Hercules, matching the city of Hercules, California.
'Lincoln' is exactly the name of Lincoln, Nebraska, and dozens of other US places.
The word 'Corona' is exactly the name of Corona, California.
'Glen Cove' is exactly the name of Glen Cove, New York (and a CA locality), though here it is already a CO feature name.
'Karr' sounds like 'Carr', as in Carr, Colorado; faint.
The word 'Lion' appears in many US feature names (Lions, Lion's Head), but no single exact match stands out.
'Platt' sounds like 'Platte', as in the Platte River / North Platte, Nebraska.
